newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London ended a choppy session dominated by nearby switches. A rebound in New York arabica futures and good trade and industry buying as well as persistent arbitrage buying against the US market lifted prices from intra-day lows. November shed $26 to close at $1,523 while January was $17 lower to finish at $1,471 a tonne. New York saw a further widening in the December/March spread aided by talk of a possible closure of a leading roasters plant in northern Florida. Traders said this underlines that the just-in-time strategy is not without problems.

There is also persistent talk of a Peruvian default of about 10,000 bags to a Jacksonville warehouse, but it is not clear whether this actually is the case. Mounting concern over scarce prompt coffee supplies gave a sharp boost to Colombian and Brazilian differentials and the current supply jitters will only begin to ease when new-crop coffee starts to flow in from Latin America. However, that may happen later than expected due to the delay in Mexico's crop and weather related delays in Guatemala and Costa Rica. At the end of the session December was 1.35 cents/lb higher at 114.90 cents/lb, while March added 95 points to close at 106.80 cents/lb.

FUNDAMENTALS - COLOMBIA - Jorge Cardenas, the head of the Colombian National Coffee Growers Association said that coffee production in CY 1996 is now estimated at 11.7 million 60-kg bags up from a previous estimate of 11.0 million bags. However, rising production costs, lower world market prices and the strengthening of the peso against the dollar have brought the coffee industry into difficulties and the National Coffee Fund is facing big losses. Finance Minister Antonio Ocampo said that due to the difficult financial situation the fund would borrow up to $100 million on foreign markets before the end of the year to help shore up its battered finances. He spoke after an emergency meeting of the policy-making National Coffee Committee, called to discuss measures aimed at saving the Coffee Fund from possible collapse because of a predicted deficit of at least 120 billion pesos for 1995/96.

BRAZIL - Brazilian coffee exports in September 1996 reached 1.14 million 60-kg bags, down from 1.54 million bags in August, the Brazilian Coffee Exporters Federation (FEBEC) said. The September figure is also down from the 1.28 million bags shipped in the same month last year, according to FEBEC statistics. Shipments in October are expected to be well above 1.5 million bags as they will include exports not made in September because of the bureaucratic delay over the so-called ICMS tax exemption.

SPAIN - Spain imported 326,437 bags of coffee in May 1996, 12 percent more than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 to 1.498 million bags, 8 percent more than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 rose by 2.22 percent to 3.225 million bags. Major suppliers of green coffee in January/May 1996 were Uganda (413,200 vs 277,500 bags), Brazil (114,600 vs 255,700 bags), Colombia (172,100 vs 144,900 bags) and Vietnam (106,100 vs 135,600 bags). The country exported 214,500 bags of coffee in January/May 1996, 43 percent more than was exported the same period in 1995. Total exports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 6.7 percent to 401,000 bags.
